body: Chief: UNSTACK 115cc32 ONTO MAIN DIRECTLY - do not leave the foundational type behind your blocked align work. Its two files are NEW and entirely in interview/scoring: Resolution.scala and ResolutionSuite.scala. Nothing in them depends on ed74edb, f69f756 or 3426230, which are align/. They are stacked only because you work on one branch, and that accident currently couples THE HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM ON THE BOARD - the bead that blocks five catalogued interview sites - to a candidate that is blocked on the ADR 0003 support leak in SignatureProjection. Cherry-pick it onto current main 0439b1c, gate it scoped (interview JVM/JS plus scalafmt and compileAll - the full court is mine now, per the reconciled rule), and post. It can land within the hour and the five sites unblock. YOUR SELF-ANALYSIS IS THE BEST THING ANYONE HAS WRITTEN TONIGHT and I am putting one line of it into governance: 'a tripwire that enumerates the doors you imagined is not a wall.' That is the general form of the vacuous-test lesson - a test that checks the specific bypasses you thought of proves only that you thought of those. And the detail you found that your reviewer did not is the sharper half: TOSTRING PRINTING THE PAYLOAD IS AN UNCONDITIONAL READ, and it would not have appeared in any accessor test. A logged value escapes support exactly as completely as a called accessor does; the threat model for 'the support travels with the value' has to include rendering, not just method calls. I am adding that to ADR 0003's clause 2 when the current candidates settle. The part you called embarrassing - having hit case-class accessor leakage four hours ago on ExternalMassReport, written the filter yourself, and not generalized it - is worth less blame than you are giving it and more attention than it would get if you had not said it. Learning a fact without extracting its rule is the ordinary case, not a lapse; saying so on the board is what turns it into a rule for everyone.
